title: Responsive token density and scroll rendering sweep — Safari / Firefox / mobile
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Scope: Full QA sweep focusing on token-driven density modes (compact/comfortable), interactive hit targets, virtualized table scrolling, and canvas/chart rendering across Safari (macOS/iOS), Firefox (desktop/mobile), and Chromium-based Android webviews. Goals: identify regressions introduced by recent token refactor (density/token-scale v2), triage by severity, provide actionable design fixes and reproducible steps for engineering, and land short-term mitigations for shipping teams.
test_matrix: macOS Safari 17 (Safari WebKit) — Desktop Retina / non-integer DPR
iOS Safari 16 / 17 — iPhone 12/13 (safe-area-insets / notch / toolbar overlay)
Firefox for Android — Android WebView interplay (momentum scroll differences)
Chrome on Android (WebView stable) — compare scroll momentum and overscroll behavior
iOS WKWebView (app) — embed scenarios where header sticky + sticky token elements overlap
acceptance_criteria: Documented repro steps for each unique bug with screen recordings and minimal repro case in the playground
Design fixes proposed (token values or CSS patterns) for each bug and reviewed by Eng lead
Severe regressions (affecting input hit-area or table row selection) assigned to eng owner with ETA
Short-term CSS workarounds landed as a patch in ui-kit if immediate fix required
Regression baseline added to visual-diff suite and a follow-up ticket created to prevent recurrence
updates: 2025-03-01 — Created ticket. Initial triage: tokens v2 rollout may have introduced fractional padding that interacts poorly with overflow:hidden in Safari; added test matrix.

2025-03-03 — Found reproducible issue: compact token spacing causes truncated touch hit targets on iOS Safari when combined with transform-based animations. Recorded 30s screen capture and attached to ticket.

2025-03-04 — Engineering feedback (ENG-41290): transform vs top/left layout changes affect stacking context and hit testing on iOS; suggested temporary CSS fallback using will-change:none + -webkit-overflow-scrolling tweaks.

2025-03-06 — Discovered chart canvas blurring in Firefox when devicePixelRatio is non-integer; likely related to canvas scaling and fractional pixel rounding. Added minimal JS repro and flagged for Eng (ENG-41322).

2025-03-07 — Virtualized table row jump on Safari when rapidly scrolling: root cause appears to be combination of sticky header + position:sticky + CSS contain:layout on list container. Proposed removing contain for table container as short-term fix.
2025-03-08 — PM review (Lina Torres): prioritize touch hit target and table selection bugs as P0 for customer-facing dashboards; charts and cosmetic subpixel issues set to P2.

2025-03-10 — Implemented and validated CSS mitigation for iOS hit targets in staging (PR: github.com/redwood/ui-kit/pull/3287). Verified fixes on iPhone 12 and 13. Added visual diff snapshots and updated acceptance criteria. Moving to In Progress — implementation phase with Eng review pending.
triage_notes: - P0: touch hit-target truncation on iOS causing missed selections in product dashboards
- P0: virtualized table selection loss on Safari during momentum scroll
- P1: chart blurring in Firefox on fractional DPR — cosmetic but affects readability for small text
- P2: minor token spacing drift in large-scale tables on Android webview

Decision log: short-term CSS mitigations where safe; engineering to own permanent fixes for overflow/contain and canvas scaling. Design to add token guidance and update Figma tokens to include recommended safe rounding rules (integer px or rem fallback).
next_steps: 1) Eng owners ENG-41290 (hit-targets) and ENG-41322 (canvas DPR) to provide ETA and link to dependent PRs
2) Land patch PR for table container contain removal and run full e2e scroll regression suite
3) Update Figma token page with explicit recommended constraints and an example 'safe-mode' token set for compact density
4) Add visual-diff baseline for affected playground pages and include them in nightly CI
5) Schedule a cross-team review (Design + Eng + PM) 2025-03-12 to confirm release gating for ui-kit-2025.04
review_feedback: PM (Lina Torres): Confirmed priority — product dashboards use case must be green before Dedicated customers are migrated.
Eng lead (Rajiv Menon): Agreed with short-term CSS mitigations; will assign owners and schedule time in next sprint.
QA (Sofia Martinez): Added additional repro steps for Firefox canvas case; suggested adding pixel-ratio sweep to automation matrix.
